answer: Each agent’s voting weight can be tied to a unique, nontransferable credential issued only after a small human-held stake is locked for a cooling period. A lagoon of accounts may appear at one address, but the tide of new identities gains no extra influence: the same stake cannot back them all at once. To amplify votes, an attacker must lock more capital and wait through each period, paying opportunity cost and risking forfeiture if caught coordinating fraud. A ferrous token alone proves nothing; the scarce, delayed credential is the defense.
